headline: Indian benchmark indices decline in early trade following global sell-off and profit taking after opening higher

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Global sell-off and profit taking after a two-day rally dragged down early trading gains.
The Indian rupee weakened 23 paise to 92.85 against the U.S. dollar in early trade.
Weak Asian and global market cues pressured domestic equities despite initial foreign inflows.
Nifty Bank snapped its two-day record rally as Sensex dropped around 200 points.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty opened higher supported by foreign inflows before turning negative later in the morning.
Tata Steel announced it will acquire a 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore.
Nifty slipped below the 25,700 level while Nifty IT index saw early gains of 1.62%.
Gold prices rebounded from a 14-month low amid focus on U.S. inflation data and Federal Reserve rate outlook.
summary: Indian benchmark indices turned negative after a higher opening, with Sensex falling 200 points and Nifty dipping below 25,700 due to global sell-offs and profit booking. The Indian rupee weakened to 92.85 against the U.S. dollar in early trading. Major news included Tata Steel announcing a ₹15,510 crore stake purchase in APL Apollo.
